review_context: distinct current Codex context; bootstrap source review only; installed product transport was not traversed

findings.message: The dedicated review credential is loaded into the network-capable broker service and passed to the broker solely so it can hash the file. This violates the intended credential separation: a compromised broker can read the bearer credential and exfiltrate or use it over its permitted DNS/HTTPS egress. The broker should receive only an expected digest; the credential itself must be mounted only into the isolated review worker.

The supervisor spawns the broker and immediately invokes the provider without waiting for a bound, policy-verified readiness signal. A normal startup race can make the first CONNECT fail, while an early broker failure is not detected until after provider execution. Require a bounded readiness handshake bound to the policy before launching the provider.

The one-use BootstrapGrant rejects every effect except coding-release, while the new deployment path is approval-platform-bootstrap-deployment. Consequently the declared one-time bootstrap authority cannot authorize the reviewed Nix generation switch; using that handler requires bypassing this one-use grant or a different unmodeled authority path. Bind the grant to the exact new typed effect and its system closure identities.

The broker trusts a JSON network-attestation file based only on self-asserted fields and an unkeyed hash checked by the consumer. No candidate source component derives or signs tgw-review-egress-network-attestation/v1 from the privileged namespace probes, yet the Nix unit requires this file. An operator or compromised unprivileged producer can assert direct_egress_denied without kernel evidence. Generate the attestation in the privileged fixed helper from exact readback/probes and authenticate its provenance.
